speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your skin condition, could you please describe the lesions you are concerned about in detail, including when they first appeared and whether they have changed in size, shape, or color?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the location and appearance of these lesions, are they painful, and have you noticed any bleeding or ulceration? I also need to ask if you have ever been screened for or diagnosed with HIV or other sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronicity, location, and failure of previous treatments, I need to rule out malignancy or a chronic viral infection. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile and finger lesions; REQUEST TEST: HPV DNA testing; REQUEST TEST: HIV testing.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy: Findings show cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. HIV: Negative. HPV DNA testing: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy findings of multinucleation and nuclear hyperchromasia are highly suggestive of a viral cytopathic effect, likely Herpes Simplex Virus, despite the negative HPV test. To confirm this specific viral etiology, I need to request immunohistochemical staining for HSV. REQUEST TEST: Immunohistochemistry for HSV-1 and HSV-2.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Immunohistochemistry for HSV-1 and HSV-2: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative HSV stains and HPV results, combined with the chronic, non-healing nature of the lesions and your smoking history, strongly suggest Squamous Cell Carcinoma rather than a viral infection. I will now request a full histopathology report to confirm the diagnosis and check for specific markers like p16. REQUEST TEST: Full histopathology report with p16 immunostaining.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Full histopathology report: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma. p16 immunostaining: Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The histopathology confirms invasive squamous cell carcinoma, and the positive p16 staining indicates an association with HPV infection. I will now request imaging to assess for regional lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. REQUEST IMAGES: CT scan of the pelvis and abdomen.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan results are pending, but the diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma is confirmed by the biopsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma
